newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy markets refocus on fundamentals after upset.
newsitem.headline: Italy markets refocus on fundamentals after upset.

text.p: Italian markets will focus on economic fundamentals in the coming weeks after gritting their teeth through the centre-left government's worst crisis to date, market analysts said on Friday.
But beneath the apparent calm, investors are under no illusions about the position of Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition and expect greater political problems ahead.

"Provided we get a few weeks of reduced political instability, the market should focus on the ongoing decline in inflation and rigorous monetary policy pursued by the Bank of Italy," said Riccardo Barbieri at Morgan Stanley in London.
Prodi's government came unexpectedly close to disaster this week after briefly losing support of its key ally, the hard left Communist Refoundation party, over sending forces to Albania.

His Olive Tree coalition made a deal with the opposition Freedom Alliance at the price of a confidence vote in both chambers. Prodi survived one vote and should win the next but analysts say his coalition's political shelf life has shortened.

"The Prodi government is weakened after this but we don't think it jeopardises the stability of the government for the next couple of months," said Lorenzo Codogno, chief economist at Bank of America here.
He saw the coalition holding its present form to the end of June when key electoral reforms would be tackled but once these were past that could be the moment for a new form of government.

Barbieri agreed that the next two or three months were crucial but did not rule out the possibility that European monetary union commitments might make it awkward for parliament to dump him within the next year.
In the short-term, the market was seen concentrating on slowing Italian inflation, with April consumer price growth expected to brake to two percent after March's 2.2 percent.
Now the lira seems to have recovered from a weak bout in Europe's currency grid, economists say markets will look for an official interest rate cut in the next month or so.
Lorenzo Stanca, economist at Credito Italiano here, saw a 75 basis point cut in the 6.75 percent discount rate in May and forecast the lira gaining on the mark to 980 from 986 today.

With little on the political agenda until the government presents its three-year plan of rolling economic targets, due in May, and the electoral reforms, Stanca said the gap between yields on fixed rate Italian government bonds and German Bunds should range between 160 and 190 basis points, from 175 today.
The government's stumbling block will be making changes to state spending on welfare and pensions. Communist Refoundation has made plain it is against spending cuts in these areas.

At this point, either in summer or autumn, analysts expect the profile of the coalition to change, with centrist parties switching from the Freedom Alliance to the government and replacing the communists, or the creation of a grand coalition.
But Stanca said the market now saw less political risk in Italy than in recent years because there was a central majority which supported reforming the social security system.
"Even in the case of a change of coalition this is not seen as an occasion for a tremendous sell off," he said.
